scenario: Two international arbitration teams, Team Alpha and Team Beta, are compared on case-resolution success rates across complex multi-party disputes and simple bilateral disputes. Team Alpha takes on mostly complex cases; Team Beta mostly handles simple ones.

data.description: Case-resolution success rates by dispute complexity

question: (a) Which team has the higher aggregate resolution rate? (b) Which team is better within each complexity tier? (c) Compute corrected rates using equal 50/50 complexity weights.

ground_truth.explanation: Team Beta's aggregate advantage disappears once dispute complexity is controlled for. Team Alpha outperforms in both strata.

naive_answer: Team Beta is superior; overall rate 0.8462 vs Alpha's 0.7087.
naive_trap: Team Alpha shoulders 87.5% complex disputes, which are intrinsically harder, severely depressing its aggregate relative to Team Beta.
reasoning_trace: Complex: Alpha 0.68 > Beta 0.61. Simple: Alpha 0.91 > Beta 0.88. Corrected: Alpha=0.795, Beta=0.745. Alpha wins.
python_verification:
nAc,rAc,nAs,rAs = 700,0.68,100,0.91
nBc,rBc,nBs,rBs = 100,0.61,700,0.88
ovA=(nAc*rAc+nAs*rAs)/(nAc+nAs); ovB=(nBc*rBc+nBs*rBs)/(nBc+nBs)
assert ovB > ovA
cA=0.5*rAc+0.5*rAs; cB=0.5*rBc+0.5*rBs
assert abs(cA-0.795)<0.005 and abs(cB-0.745)<0.005
assert cA > cB
